englishTitle: Money Can Buy Love After All
countingMethod: Substantive text blocks = narrative/answer paragraphs + bold interviewer prompts + section headings; H1, subtitle, byline, date, captions, placeholders and the archival footer excluded.
completenessChecks: First and last paragraphs compared with source-record completeness fields.
Every interviewer prompt present, bold, in its own paragraph, in order.
Every answer paragraph present with original boundaries and quotation marks.
Section headings, captions and photo credits present in original positions.
Hyperlinks from the Hebrew body kept on the same words.
Names, numbers, dates and titles checked against the Hebrew; nothing silently corrected.
Block-sequence alignment script run: paragraph/prompt/heading sequence matches the Hebrew (H1 omitted by design).
voiceChecks: Long-then-short rhythm kept; one-word and short verdict sentences preserved as short sentences.
Parentheticals kept as parentheticals with their function (gloss, deflation, confession).
Mock-honorifics, epithets and deadpan understatement rendered at the same weight; no intensifiers added.
No jokes added, explained or removed; no transitions or conclusions appended.
Present-tense narration kept; Hebrew verb-first and subject-dropped sentences recast as natural English without reordering content.
Interviewee quotations translated from the published Hebrew only; no reconstruction of original English speech.
decisions: Title: 'כסף כן יכול לקנות אהבה' rendered 'Money Can Buy Love After All' to carry the emphatic כן; citation gloss remains 'Money can buy love'.
'שוק הפו"פ' (פנים אל פנים, first in-person dates) rendered 'first-date market'; caption likewise.
Show title rendered with the established English name The Millionaire Matchmaker.
'בלבוסטה' kept as 'balabusta' (profile guidance); 'בחורה כלבבי' rendered 'a girl after my own heart'.
Publisher paragraph split mid-sentence ('אני' / 'חושבת') joined into one paragraph; hence 17 translated blocks against 18 source blocks.
sourceProblems: Source promotes a longer print interview in Pnai Plus that was not recovered; this is the online edition only.
Source record confirms the bold caption 'שוק הפו"פ בידיה' is a caption, not a prompt.
